raw_comment:
1) Until 2022-23, the winter months were often the busiest for doctor and hospital visits for respiratory diseases. Pre-pandemic visits were roughly 5.5% from late December to January. The year 2022-23 is notable, with occurrences increasing much earlier, from October to December - from around 2.5% to over 7.5%, the highest point on the curve. I notice there is a triple peak in the 2019-2020 season around 7%. 

2) Did prior years' diseases such as influenza, covid 19, and so on have long-term consequences on the respiratory system, influencing the 2022-2023 report? I'm curious why the lowest percentage of weekly doctor and hospital visits occurred in 2020-21, when it was intended to be the peak of Covid-19. Why is there a triple peak for the 2019-2020 season? I wonder if immunities gained from the pandemic had an impact on doctor visits post-pandemic.

3) During the winter season, disease seems to afflict the planet, and it is easy to witness sickness in high school. Masks are uncommon at this stage after the epidemic, and it's strange to feel as though disease surrounds me and I'm at the eye of the storm. Relatives of mine have had tremendous difficulty overcoming illnesses brought on by weather and transmuted by pathogens from coworkers. As someone who has had to constantly observe and be a patient at the doctor's and hospital, it's intriguing to find me amid a sea of individuals who are similar to me.

4) The Doctor's In! A History of Respiratory Illness Fluctuations

And the only times we were really allowed out was whenever we had to rush to the hospital (for a REAL emergency) or for grocery shopping.

What do you notice?
I noticed that once the pandemic picked up, and after it, hospital visits increased drastically for respiratory illness. While some may have thought the highest percentages would have been from 2019-2020, the percentages in 2022-2023 reach nearly 8%, which is way higher compared to the other years.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why the rates of respiratory illnesses are higher now that the pandemic spoken isn't about as much and why the rates are higher in the colder months. I wonder what the exact reason behind the peaks are. Were they because of COVID or other reasons?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because many people got sick and the hospitals had lots of people to assist. Some people may have gotten sicker being in the hospitals. Many people also had to fight off covid and prevent it from being brought to their houses, which may have influenced the decrease in some peaks. However, those who have gotten covid claim activities have been more difficult as they lose their breaths much quicker, which influences the peaks in the graph.

I noticed that the 2019-20 weekly visit was the highest in late December through the end of April. Than the average had decreased exponentially with an all time low throughout 2020-21. Then during the early winter months of 2021-22 the percentage had spiked again, before decreasing gradually. Then the 2022-23 percentage thus far had continued to increase to an all time high. 

I wonder why the pre-pandemic average weekly doctor visits was higher than the 2020-21 average. I also wonder why the 2022-23 weekly doctor visit was higher than all of the previous COVID years. 

I observe that the peak of the 2019-20 peak percentages correspond to the beginnings of the Coronavirus pandemic. Thus the weekly doctors visits may have been higher before the nationwide quarantine was put into place early March. This was likely why the doctors visits continued to be low throughout 2020-21. Then in the early winter of 2021-22, the respiratory illnesses spiked again, corresponding with another rise in Covid. The early winter was also shown to be the time that the average pre-pandemic respiratory illnesses spiked. The 2022-23 respiratory illnesses has been the highest than it has ever been earlier than average. This could be because people's respiratory systems had been weakened from the pandemic, resulting in being more susceptible to respiratory illnesses.

In my own community I have seen a rise in colds earlier than normal, for the winter season.
